contentHtml:
Use this book when changing behavior inside an application. Start with a decision the software must make, identify the module that owns it and follow one change through every caller that can produce the same effect.

Where to start

When you need to… Read
Agree on what users should observe Spec-driven development
Decide which service owns the data Boundaries and service design
Implement one rule shared by an endpoint and a worker Business rule placement
Define what callers can depend on and how they handle failures Module boundaries, dependencies and errors
Move a duplicated booking rule one caller at a time Safely refactoring a shared booking rule
Record the expected results and evidence Test case standards

Applying the standard

For an implementation or review, write down the business rule in one sentence. Name the operation that owns it, the callers that invoke it, the write that enforces it and the test that would expose a violation. Use the module and naming conventions already present in the application.

For example, ask a coding assistant to read the placement chapter, trace the existing reservation paths, then implement the last-slot rule through their shared operation. Ask it to show the result for each caller when two customers compete for that slot.

See the references for the reasoning behind these defaults.
